name: Malaria
description: Mosquito-borne parasitic infection caused by Plasmodium species, endemic across much of Kenya, especially western and coastal regions.
keySymptoms: cyclical fever with chills and sweating
recent travel to or residence in a malaria-endemic area
riskFactors: living in or travel to an endemic region
warningSigns: very high fever in a child
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing and treatment immediately with any fever after travel to or residence in a malaria-endemic area; severe malaria can progress within hours, especially in children and pregnant women.

name: Typhoid Fever
description: Systemic bacterial infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, spread through contaminated food or water.
keySymptoms: stepwise rising fever over several days
warningSigns: severe abdominal pain and rigidity (possible perforation)
persistent high fever beyond a week
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for testing if fever persists more than 3 days, especially with abdominal pain; can cause serious complications if untreated.

name: Tuberculosis (Pulmonary)
description: Chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily affecting the lungs; a major public health concern in Kenya.
keySymptoms: cough lasting more than 2 weeks with weight loss and night sweats
riskFactors: close contact with a TB patient
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation and sputum testing for any cough lasting more than 2 weeks, particularly with weight loss or night sweats.

name: HIV (Acute Retroviral Syndrome)
description: Early symptomatic phase after HIV infection, occurring 2-4 weeks post-exposure.
keySymptoms: flu-like illness following a recent high-risk exposure
whenToSeekCare: Testing is recommended for anyone with a recent possible exposure and flu-like symptoms; early diagnosis allows early treatment.

name: Cholera
description: Acute diarrheal infection caused by Vibrio cholerae, transmitted through contaminated water; occurs in outbreaks in parts of Kenya.
keySymptoms: large-volume 'rice water' watery diarrhea with rapid dehydration
warningSigns: signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, no tears, little urine, lethargy)
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency rehydration care immediately; cholera can cause fatal dehydration within hours if untreated.

name: Bacterial Pneumonia
description: Lung infection, commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, presenting with fever and productive cough.
keySymptoms: fever with productive cough and pleuritic chest pain
warningSigns: chest pain that worsens with breathing
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical care for fever with cough and breathing difficulty, especially in young children or the elderly.

name: Common Cold (Viral URI)
description: Mild self-limiting viral infection of the upper respiratory tract.
warningSigns: symptoms lasting more than 10 days or worsening
whenToSeekCare: Usually resolves on its own within a week with rest and fluids; seek care if symptoms worsen or persist.

name: Influenza
description: Viral respiratory illness that is typically more severe than the common cold, with abrupt onset.
keySymptoms: abrupt onset of high fever with body aches
whenToSeekCare: Rest and fluids for most cases; seek care if breathing difficulty or high fever persists beyond a few days.

name: COVID-19
description: Respiratory illness caused by SARS-CoV-2, ranging from mild to severe presentations.
keySymptoms: loss of taste or smell
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Isolate and monitor for mild cases; seek emergency care immediately for breathing difficulty or chest pain.

name: Measles
description: Highly contagious viral illness with characteristic rash, still seen in under-vaccinated communities.
keySymptoms: fever followed by a rash spreading from the face downward
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
warningSigns: signs of pneumonia or encephalitis (confusion, seizures)
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care promptly, especially in unvaccinated children; complications can be serious.

name: Chickenpox (Varicella)
description: Contagious viral infection causing an itchy blistering rash, common in childhood.
keySymptoms: itchy rash progressing through spots, blisters, and crusts
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
warningSigns: signs of skin infection (spreading redness, pus)
high fever persisting beyond a few days
whenToSeekCare: Usually mild and self-limiting; seek care if the rash becomes infected or if breathing difficulty develops.

name: Mumps
description: Viral infection causing painful swelling of the salivary glands.
keySymptoms: swelling of the parotid gland below the ear
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Usually resolves with rest; seek care for severe pain, testicular swelling, or neurological symptoms.

name: Rubella (German Measles)
description: Mild viral illness of concern mainly due to risk to unborn babies if contracted during pregnancy.
keySymptoms: mild fever with rash and swollen lymph nodes behind the ears
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
warningSigns: exposure during pregnancy warrants urgent evaluation
whenToSeekCare: Usually mild in children and adults; pregnant women exposed to rubella should seek care promptly.

name: Hepatitis A
description: Viral liver infection spread through contaminated food or water, usually self-limiting.
keySymptoms: jaundice with dark urine following gastrointestinal symptoms
whenToSeekCare: Most cases resolve with rest and supportive care; seek care if jaundice is severe or confusion develops.

name: Hepatitis B
description: Viral liver infection that can become chronic and lead to long-term liver damage.
warningSigns: signs of liver failure (confusion, severe jaundice, bleeding)
whenToSeekCare: Testing is recommended for at-risk individuals; chronic infection needs long-term specialist follow-up.

name: Hepatitis C
description: Viral liver infection often asymptomatic initially but can cause chronic liver disease.
warningSigns: signs of advanced liver disease (jaundice, swelling, confusion)
whenToSeekCare: Often silent for years; testing is advised for those with known risk factors.

name: Bacterial Meningitis
description: Serious bacterial infection of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
keySymptoms: stiff neck with fever and severe headache
whenToSeekCare: This is a medical emergency — seek immediate care for fever with stiff neck and severe headache.

name: Viral Meningitis
description: Inflammation of the meninges caused by a virus, generally milder than bacterial meningitis.
whenToSeekCare: Needs urgent evaluation to rule out the more dangerous bacterial form.

name: Urinary Tract Infection
description: Bacterial infection of the bladder or urinary tract, common especially in women.
keySymptoms: burning pain on urination with urinary frequency
warningSigns: fever with chills and flank pain (possible kidney infection)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for testing and treatment; untreated infections can spread to the kidneys.

name: Shigellosis (Bacterial Dysentery)
description: Bacterial intestinal infection causing bloody diarrhea, spread via contaminated food or water.
keySymptoms: bloody, mucoid diarrhea with cramping
whenToSeekCare: Seek care for bloody diarrhea, especially in young children; dehydration can develop quickly.

name: Amoebiasis
description: Parasitic intestinal infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica, spread through contaminated food or water.
warningSigns: signs of liver abscess (right upper abdominal pain, fever)
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing and treatment for persistent or bloody diarrhea.

name: Giardiasis
description: Parasitic intestinal infection causing prolonged diarrhea, spread via contaminated water.
keySymptoms: prolonged foul-smelling, greasy diarrhea
warningSigns: symptoms lasting more than two weeks
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for testing if diarrhea persists beyond a week or two.

name: Brucellosis
description: Bacterial infection acquired from unpasteurized dairy or contact with infected livestock, common in pastoral regions.
keySymptoms: recurring or undulating fever with joint pain and livestock/unpasteurized dairy exposure
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing if fever persists with a history of unpasteurized dairy or animal contact.

name: Leptospirosis
description: Bacterial infection from water or soil contaminated with animal urine, often after flooding.
keySymptoms: fever with severe calf muscle pain after exposure to floodwater
whenToSeekCare: Seek care for fever with muscle pain after flood or contaminated water exposure; can progress to severe organ involvement.

name: Rabies
description: Fatal viral infection transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal, almost always preventable with prompt treatment.
keySymptoms: animal bite or scratch followed by tingling/pain at the wound site
warningSigns: any bite or scratch from a suspected rabid animal requires immediate post-exposure treatment
whenToSeekCare: Wash the wound immediately and seek emergency post-exposure treatment right away — rabies is fatal once symptoms begin, but is preventable if treated promptly after exposure.

name: Tetanus
description: Bacterial infection causing muscle rigidity and spasms, entering through wounds.
keySymptoms: jaw and neck stiffness after a wound, especially if unvaccinated
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for any deep or contaminated wound, especially with incomplete tetanus vaccination.

name: Diphtheria
description: Serious bacterial throat infection that can obstruct breathing, preventable by vaccination.
keySymptoms: thick gray membrane in the throat
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately; diphtheria can rapidly obstruct the airway.

name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
description: Highly contagious bacterial respiratory infection causing severe coughing fits, most dangerous in infants.
keySymptoms: coughing fits followed by a high-pitched 'whoop' sound
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care for infants with severe coughing fits — this can be life-threatening in young babies.

name: Otitis Media (Ear Infection)
description: Middle ear infection, common in young children, often following a cold.
keySymptoms: ear pain with fever, often following a cold
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician if ear pain persists more than a day or two, or if there's discharge or fever.

name: Streptococcal Pharyngitis (Strep Throat)
description: Bacterial throat infection that can lead to complications if untreated.
keySymptoms: sudden severe sore throat with fever and no cough
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for testing; untreated strep can lead to rheumatic fever or kidney complications.

name: Scabies
description: Contagious skin infestation caused by mites, causing intense itching.
commonSymptoms: rash in web spaces of fingers
keySymptoms: intense nighttime itching with rash between fingers
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
warningSigns: signs of secondary bacterial skin infection (spreading redness, pus, fever)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for treatment; household and close contacts often need treatment too.

name: Ringworm (Tinea)
description: Fungal skin infection causing a ring-shaped itchy rash.
keySymptoms: ring-shaped rash with a clearer center
riskFactors: close contact with infected persons or animals
warningSigns: widespread or worsening rash despite treatment
whenToSeekCare: Usually treatable with antifungal medication; see a clinician if it doesn't improve or spreads.

name: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye)
description: Inflammation of the eye's outer membrane, caused by infection or irritation.
whenToSeekCare: Usually resolves on its own or with drops; seek care if vision is affected or pain is severe.

name: Impetigo
description: Contagious bacterial skin infection common in children, causing honey-colored crusted sores.
commonSymptoms: red sores that ooze and crust
lessCommonSymptoms: swollen lymph nodes near the sores
keySymptoms: honey-colored crusted sores, often around the nose and mouth
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for topical or oral antibiotics; keep affected areas clean to prevent spread.

name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
description: Chronic condition of elevated blood pressure, often with no symptoms until complications arise.
warningSigns: difficulty speaking (possible hypertensive emergency or stroke)
whenToSeekCare: Regular blood pressure checks are important since it's often silent; seek immediate care for very high readings with symptoms.

name: Type 2 Diabetes
description: Chronic metabolic condition of high blood sugar, increasingly common with rising obesity rates.
keySymptoms: excessive thirst and urination with unexplained fatigue
warningSigns: very high or very low blood sugar symptoms
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for blood sugar testing; untreated diabetes leads to serious long-term complications.

name: Type 1 Diabetes
description: Autoimmune condition causing insulin deficiency, usually presenting in childhood or young adulthood.
keySymptoms: rapid weight loss with excessive thirst and urination, often in a child or young adult
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent evaluation for new excessive thirst and weight loss in a child or young adult.

name: Asthma
description: Chronic condition causing airway inflammation and episodic breathing difficulty.
keySymptoms: recurrent wheezing and breathlessness, often triggered by exercise, cold air, or allergens
riskFactors: family history of asthma or allergies
exposure to smoke or air pollution
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for severe breathing difficulty; work with a clinician on a long-term management plan.

name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
description: Progressive lung disease causing airflow limitation, strongly linked to smoking and indoor air pollution.
keySymptoms: progressive breathlessness with a long history of smoking or biomass smoke exposure
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for lung function testing; seek emergency care for sudden worsening of breathing.

name: Coronary Artery Disease / Angina
description: Narrowing of the heart's blood vessels causing chest pain, especially with exertion.
commonSymptoms: chest pain or pressure with exertion
lessCommonSymptoms: pain radiating to the arm or jaw
keySymptoms: chest pressure brought on by exertion and relieved by rest
warningSigns: chest pain at rest lasting more than a few minutes
pain radiating to the arm, jaw, or back
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for chest pain at rest — this could indicate a heart attack.

name: Heart Failure
description: Condition where the heart cannot pump blood effectively, leading to fluid buildup.
lessCommonSymptoms: rapid weight gain from fluid retention
keySymptoms: breathlessness that worsens when lying flat, with leg swelling
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for new or worsening breathlessness and swelling.

name: Stroke
description: Sudden interruption of blood supply to the brain, causing focal neurological deficits.
keySymptoms: sudden one-sided weakness or facial drooping with slurred speech
warningSigns: any sudden weakness, facial drooping, or speech difficulty is a medical emergency
whenToSeekCare: Call for emergency help immediately — every minute matters for stroke treatment outcomes.

name: Chronic Kidney Disease
description: Progressive loss of kidney function, often linked to diabetes and hypertension.
warningSigns: very little or no urine output
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for kidney function testing, especially with diabetes or hypertension; seek urgent care for the warning signs above.

name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
description: Sores in the stomach or upper intestine lining, often linked to H. pylori infection or NSAID use.
commonSymptoms: pain relieved or worsened by eating
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care for vomiting blood or black stools — these can indicate bleeding.

name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
description: Chronic acid reflux causing heartburn and regurgitation.
warningSigns: chest pain that could be cardiac in origin
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician if symptoms are frequent or if any warning signs are present.

name: Migraine
description: Recurrent moderate to severe headache disorder, often with associated nausea and light sensitivity.
keySymptoms: throbbing one-sided headache with nausea and light sensitivity
warningSigns: headache with fever and stiff neck
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for recurrent migraines to discuss triggers and treatment; the warning signs above need emergency evaluation.

name: Tension Headache
description: Common headache type causing a band-like pressure sensation, often stress-related.
warningSigns: sudden severe headache unlike usual pattern
headache with fever and stiff neck
whenToSeekCare: Usually manageable with rest and over-the-counter pain relief; see a clinician if headaches become frequent or severe.

name: Osteoarthritis
description: Degenerative joint disease causing pain and stiffness, common with aging.
warningSigns: sudden severe joint swelling with fever (possible infection)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for persistent joint pain to discuss management options.

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
description: Autoimmune condition causing joint inflammation, typically affecting multiple joints symmetrically.
commonSymptoms: morning stiffness lasting over an hour
keySymptoms: symmetrical joint swelling with prolonged morning stiffness
warningSigns: chest pain or breathlessness (possible lung/heart involvement)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for evaluation; early treatment helps prevent joint damage.

name: Gout
description: Form of arthritis caused by uric acid crystal buildup, often affecting the big toe.
commonSymptoms: sudden severe joint pain (often big toe)
keySymptoms: sudden severe pain, redness, and swelling of the big toe
warningSigns: fever with joint swelling (possible joint infection)
inability to move the affected joint
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for confirmation and treatment; recurrent attacks need long-term management.

name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
description: Reduced red blood cell count due to insufficient iron, common especially in women and children.
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for blood testing; treatable with iron supplementation once the cause is identified.

name: Hypothyroidism
description: Underactive thyroid gland causing slowed metabolism.
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for thyroid function testing if symptoms are persistent.

name: Hyperthyroidism
description: Overactive thyroid gland causing accelerated metabolism.
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for thyroid function testing; seek emergency care for the warning signs above.

name: Epilepsy
description: Neurological condition characterized by recurrent seizures.
keySymptoms: recurrent unprovoked seizures
warningSigns: repeated seizures without recovery between them
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for a first seizure or one lasting more than 5 minutes; ongoing epilepsy needs specialist follow-up.

name: Sickle Cell Disease Crisis
description: Acute painful episode in people with sickle cell disease, caused by blocked blood flow.
keySymptoms: severe pain crisis in a known sickle cell patient
riskFactors: sickle cell trait in both parents
warningSigns: chest pain with breathlessness (possible acute chest syndrome)
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt care for a pain crisis, and emergency care for chest pain, high fever, or stroke-like symptoms.

name: Pre-eclampsia
description: Pregnancy complication involving high blood pressure and organ involvement, usually after 20 weeks.
keySymptoms: new high blood pressure with headache and visual changes after 20 weeks of pregnancy
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency obstetric care immediately for these symptoms during pregnancy — this can become life-threatening quickly.

name: Gestational Diabetes
description: Diabetes that develops during pregnancy, usually resolving after delivery.
warningSigns: signs of very high or very low blood sugar
whenToSeekCare: Routine screening during pregnancy is important; work with a clinician on diet and monitoring.

name: Postpartum Hemorrhage
description: Excessive bleeding after childbirth, a leading cause of maternal mortality.
keySymptoms: heavy bleeding soon after childbirth
whenToSeekCare: This is a medical emergency — seek immediate care for heavy bleeding after childbirth.

name: Ectopic Pregnancy
description: Pregnancy implanted outside the uterus, most often in the fallopian tube; life-threatening if it ruptures.
keySymptoms: one-sided pelvic pain with vaginal bleeding and a positive pregnancy test
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for pelvic pain with a positive pregnancy test — rupture can be life-threatening.

name: Miscarriage (Threatened/Incomplete Abortion)
description: Pregnancy loss before 20 weeks, presenting with bleeding and cramping.
warningSigns: heavy bleeding (soaking a pad an hour)
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for any bleeding in pregnancy.

name: Puerperal Sepsis
description: Infection of the genital tract occurring after childbirth.
keySymptoms: fever with foul-smelling discharge in the days after delivery
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately — this can progress rapidly to life-threatening sepsis.

name: Mastitis
description: Painful inflammation of breast tissue, common during breastfeeding.
keySymptoms: localized breast redness and pain with fever in a breastfeeding mother
warningSigns: abscess formation (a painful lump that doesn't improve)
whenToSeekCare: Continue breastfeeding/pumping if possible and see a clinician promptly if fever or worsening redness develops.

name: Neonatal Jaundice
description: Yellowing of a newborn's skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin, common in the first week of life.
keySymptoms: yellow skin appearing in the first days of life
warningSigns: jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt evaluation for any newborn jaundice — severe untreated jaundice can cause lasting harm.

name: Neonatal Sepsis
description: Serious bloodstream infection in a newborn, requiring urgent treatment.
keySymptoms: a newborn who is unusually sleepy or feeding poorly, with abnormal temperature
riskFactors: prolonged rupture of membranes before delivery
warningSigns: any of the common symptoms above in a newborn warrant emergency evaluation
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for a newborn who is feeding poorly, unusually sleepy, or has an abnormal temperature.

name: Childhood Malnutrition (Marasmus/Kwashiorkor)
description: Severe acute malnutrition in children, presenting as either severe wasting or swelling from protein deficiency.
keySymptoms: visible severe wasting or bilateral leg swelling in a child
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care at a health facility — severe acute malnutrition needs specialized feeding and monitoring.

name: Diarrheal Disease with Dehydration (Children)
description: Acute diarrhea in a child leading to fluid loss, a major cause of child illness.
keySymptoms: signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, dry mouth, reduced urination, lethargy
warningSigns: very little or no urine output
skin that stays pinched when pressed
whenToSeekCare: Start oral rehydration immediately and seek care promptly, especially if any warning signs of dehydration appear.

name: Acute Respiratory Infection (Children)
description: Common childhood respiratory illness ranging from mild cold symptoms to pneumonia.
keySymptoms: fast or labored breathing in a child
warningSigns: chest indrawing (skin pulling in with each breath)
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care for any of the warning signs — these can indicate pneumonia.

name: Febrile Seizures
description: Seizures triggered by fever, common in young children between 6 months and 5 years.
keySymptoms: seizure occurring with a high fever in a young child
warningSigns: the child not returning to normal afterward
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation after a febrile seizure, and emergency care if it lasts more than 5 minutes.

name: Vitamin A Deficiency
description: Micronutrient deficiency affecting vision and immune function, common in undernourished children.
keySymptoms: difficulty seeing in dim light in a child
warningSigns: corneal clouding or ulceration (risk of permanent vision loss)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician promptly — vitamin A deficiency can cause irreversible eye damage if untreated.

name: Rickets
description: Bone-softening condition in children due to vitamin D or calcium deficiency.
riskFactors: dark skin with low sun exposure
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for evaluation and vitamin D/calcium supplementation.

name: Anemia in Pregnancy
description: Low red blood cell count during pregnancy, common due to increased iron demands.
whenToSeekCare: Routine antenatal screening and iron supplementation are important; seek care for severe symptoms.

name: Major Depressive Disorder
description: Persistent low mood and loss of interest that interferes with daily functioning.
keySymptoms: persistent low mood or loss of interest lasting most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks or more
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a healthcare provider or counselor — depression is treatable. If there are thoughts of self-harm, seek help immediately.

name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
description: Persistent excessive worry that is difficult to control and interferes with daily life.
keySymptoms: excessive, hard-to-control worry most days for six months or more
warningSigns: panic attacks with chest pain (need to rule out cardiac causes)
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a healthcare provider or counselor — anxiety disorders respond well to treatment.

name: Postpartum Depression
description: Depression occurring after childbirth, distinct from the milder and more common 'baby blues.'
lessCommonSymptoms: loss of interest in usual activities
keySymptoms: persistent low mood beyond two weeks after delivery, interfering with caring for the baby
warningSigns: thoughts of harming herself or the baby
inability to care for the baby
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a healthcare provider promptly — postpartum depression is common and treatable. Seek immediate help for thoughts of self-harm.

name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
description: Condition that can develop after experiencing or witnessing a traumatic event.
keySymptoms: recurrent distressing memories or flashbacks of a traumatic event
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a mental health professional — trauma-focused therapy can be very effective.

name: Panic Disorder
description: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with intense fear and physical symptoms.
keySymptoms: sudden episodes of intense fear peaking within minutes, with physical symptoms
warningSigns: chest pain needs to be evaluated to rule out cardiac causes, especially on a first episode
whenToSeekCare: See a healthcare provider — first-time chest pain or breathlessness should be medically evaluated before assuming it is panic-related.

name: Alcohol Use Disorder
description: Pattern of alcohol use causing impairment or distress, ranging from mild to severe.
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a healthcare provider — withdrawal from heavy alcohol use can be medically dangerous and should be managed with support.

name: Substance Use Disorder
description: Pattern of drug use causing significant impairment or distress.
warningSigns: overdose symptoms (unresponsiveness, slowed or stopped breathing)
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a healthcare provider for support and treatment options; seek emergency care for any overdose symptoms.

name: Bipolar Disorder
description: Condition involving alternating episodes of depression and mania or hypomania.
commonSymptoms: periods of low mood alternating with periods of elevated mood/energy
decreased need for sleep during high periods
keySymptoms: distinct episodes of unusually elevated mood and energy alternating with depression
whenToSeekCare: Speak with a mental health professional for diagnosis and treatment planning; seek immediate help for the warning signs above.

name: Psychosis / Schizophrenia Spectrum
description: Conditions involving a loss of contact with reality, including hallucinations and delusions.
keySymptoms: hallucinations or fixed false beliefs not shared by others
warningSigns: thoughts of harming self or others
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt evaluation by a mental health professional — early treatment improves outcomes significantly.

name: Insomnia
description: Persistent difficulty falling or staying asleep, affecting daytime functioning.
riskFactors: caffeine or screen use before bed
whenToSeekCare: Good sleep habits often help; see a healthcare provider if insomnia persists beyond a few weeks.

name: Grief / Adjustment Disorder
description: Emotional distress in response to loss or a major life change.
riskFactors: recent loss or major life change
warningSigns: inability to function for an extended period
whenToSeekCare: Support from friends, family, or a counselor can help; seek immediate help for thoughts of self-harm.

name: Suicidal Crisis
description: An acute state in which a person is experiencing thoughts of ending their life; always requires an immediate, compassionate response.
commonSymptoms: expressing thoughts of not wanting to live
lessCommonSymptoms: sudden calm after a period of depression
keySymptoms: any expressed thoughts or plans of suicide
warningSigns: any expression of suicidal thoughts or a plan is an emergency
whenToSeekCare: This needs immediate help — contact a crisis line, go to the nearest emergency department, or call emergency services. Do not leave the person alone.

name: Dengue Fever
description: Mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever and severe body pain, increasingly reported in Kenya.
keySymptoms: high fever with severe joint/muscle pain and pain behind the eyes
riskFactors: previous dengue infection (raises risk of severe dengue)
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care for high fever with severe body pain; watch closely for warning signs, which can indicate severe dengue.

name: Schistosomiasis (Bilharzia)
description: Parasitic infection from contact with freshwater containing infected snails, common near lakes and rivers.
keySymptoms: blood in urine with a history of freshwater exposure (lakes, rivers, irrigation canals)
riskFactors: swimming or wading in freshwater in endemic areas
warningSigns: signs of liver or kidney involvement
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for testing if there's blood in urine/stool with freshwater exposure history.

name: Soil-Transmitted Helminths (Hookworm, Ascariasis)
description: Intestinal worm infections from contact with contaminated soil, common where sanitation is limited.
warningSigns: signs of severe anemia (marked pallor, breathlessness)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for deworming treatment; heavy infestations can cause anemia and malnutrition, especially in children.

name: Onchocerciasis (River Blindness)
description: Parasitic infection spread by blackfly bites near fast-flowing rivers, which can lead to vision loss.
keySymptoms: intense itching with skin nodules near a river-dwelling area
riskFactors: living near fast-flowing rivers in endemic areas
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for evaluation and treatment; vision-related symptoms need prompt assessment to prevent permanent damage.

name: Lymphatic Filariasis (Elephantiasis)
description: Parasitic infection spread by mosquitoes, which can cause chronic limb or genital swelling.
keySymptoms: progressive limb swelling with recurrent fever, in an endemic area
riskFactors: mosquito exposure in endemic coastal areas
warningSigns: signs of skin infection over swollen areas (spreading redness, high fever)
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for evaluation and management; early treatment can prevent progression.

name: Yellow Fever
description: Mosquito-borne viral illness that can progress to severe liver and bleeding complications.
keySymptoms: fever with jaundice following mosquito exposure in an endemic area
riskFactors: travel to or residence in endemic areas
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate medical care for fever with jaundice, especially without prior yellow fever vaccination.

name: Chikungunya
description: Mosquito-borne viral illness causing high fever and severe joint pain.
keySymptoms: sudden fever with severe, often disabling, joint pain
warningSigns: signs of neurological involvement (confusion, severe headache)
whenToSeekCare: Seek care for fever with severe joint pain; joint symptoms can persist for weeks to months.

name: Rift Valley Fever
description: Viral illness affecting livestock and humans, transmitted through contact with infected animals or mosquito bites.
keySymptoms: fever after contact with sick livestock or their body fluids
riskFactors: mosquito exposure in endemic pastoral areas
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical care for fever following livestock contact during a known outbreak period.

name: Anthrax (Cutaneous)
description: Bacterial infection from contact with infected livestock or contaminated animal products.
commonSymptoms: painless skin sore with black center
keySymptoms: painless ulcer with a black center after contact with livestock
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical care for any skin sore after livestock contact, particularly during a known outbreak.

name: Trachoma
description: Bacterial eye infection and a leading cause of preventable blindness, linked to poor hygiene and water access.
whenToSeekCare: See a clinician for evaluation; repeated infections can lead to scarring and vision loss if untreated.

name: Tungiasis (Jiggers)
description: Skin infestation by burrowing sand fleas, common in areas with poor sanitation and dusty soil.
commonSymptoms: itchy swelling, usually on the feet
visible small black dot at the center of the lesion
lessCommonSymptoms: multiple lesions on toes or soles
keySymptoms: itchy lesion on the foot with a visible black central dot
riskFactors: walking barefoot on dusty or sandy soil
living in an endemic rural area
warningSigns: signs of secondary bacterial infection (spreading redness, pus, fever)
whenToSeekCare: See a health worker for safe removal; untreated lesions can become infected.

name: Snake Bite Envenomation
description: Injury from a venomous snake bite, which can cause tissue damage, bleeding problems, or paralysis depending on the species.
commonSymptoms: pain and swelling at the bite site
keySymptoms: snake bite with progressive swelling or systemic symptoms
riskFactors: living or working in rural/bush areas
warningSigns: bleeding from gums or old wounds
whenToSeekCare: Keep the person calm and still, keep the bitten limb below heart level, and get to a medical facility immediately — do not cut the wound or apply a tourniquet.

name: Heat Stroke
description: Life-threatening rise in body temperature from heat exposure, overwhelming the body's cooling ability.
keySymptoms: very high body temperature with confusion after heat exposure
whenToSeekCare: This is a medical emergency — move the person to a cool place, cool them with water/fanning, and seek emergency care immediately.
